name: Working Memory Store
purpose: i34 Tier-1 build (D-0090/D-0096/D-0077): the per-task WORKING-MEMORY STORE that MEMORY_CONTRACT Amendment A5 (U3') fully specified and RESERVED but did not build. Holds a task's evolving intermediate STATE across its iterative turns so a deepening task distinguishes its OWN current state from stale earlier state (the mechanical cure for iterative-prompt deterioration), kept STRICTLY out of long-term evidence + execution authority. A `working` record (lifeorch.memory_record/0.1, record_kind=working) is CONTINUITY-authoritative -- content_role=working_state, can_instruct=false; permissions live ONLY in a packet control_plane, never here. SQLite-backed store (working_state/0.1 sub-contract, SCHEMA_NOTES.md): immutable versioned snapshots; CAS on parent_state_version (stale-parent write FAILS CLOSED); exactly ONE active head per task_id; explicit fork; a SEPARATE fixed working-memory budget; a closed/archived state is not returned by get_active_head; PROMOTION emits a NEW derived long-term summary record (derives_from the working record, provenance_mode=derived_record) and NEVER re-labels the working record. CONJUNCTIVE isolation (task_id AND current-namespace authorization) -- the namespace half reuses #37's ONE canonical ns_permitted (imported READ-ONLY, A5 risk-6; never re-implemented); a cross-namespace access is fail-closed + sanitized (a namespace_violation_count only; identifying detail -> a privileged local security log). Ordinary search REJECTS record_kind=working (retrievable ONLY by an exact-task_id op). The compiler #40 consults get_active_head to render the packet working_memory region. Thin pwsh wrapper over a deterministic stdlib-only Python worker (working_memory.py); every emitted id/hash is content-derived -> canonical records byte-identical on a re-run of the same op sequence. CPU-only, no model, no network. NON-GOALS (later): packet assembly (#40), promotion POLICY/triggers/consolidation (Tier 2), embeddings, model use.

invocation.args_spec: Named params: -Op put_state|get_active_head|list_by_task|fork|close|archive|promote|search. put_state: -TaskId -NamespaceScope(required for v1) -Body <json|path> [-ParentStateVersion n]. get_active_head|list_by_task|close|archive|promote: -TaskId. fork: -SourceTaskId -NewTaskId. search: [-RecordKind]. All access-controlled ops take -AllowedNamespaces (request) + -PermissionGrants (grant). OR generic -InputsJson '<json {op, task_id, namespace_scope, body, parent_state_version, source_task_id, new_task_id, allowed_namespaces, permission_grants, record_kind, grant_snapshot_ref, created_from_packet_id, writer_authority, store_path, ns_policy_path, python_path, worker_path}>'. Also -StorePath (persistent; default runtime/store/working_memory.db), -NsPolicyPath, -PythonPath, -WorkerPath, -ArtifactRoot, -InvocationId.

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: put_state | get_active_head | list_by_task | fork | close | archive | promote | search.

inputs.name: task_id
inputs.description: The task whose working state this op addresses (exact match; the task-isolation half of conjunctive access).

inputs.name: namespace_scope
inputs.description: put_state (a task's v1): the isolation namespace stamped on the task's state; immutable across its versions (never widened).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: put_state: the state payload (an opaque canonical object) under the working-memory budget.

inputs.name: parent_state_version
inputs.description: put_state: the CAS token -- must equal the current active head's state_version (null/0 for a task's v1); a mismatch FAILS CLOSED (cas_conflict).

inputs.name: source_task_id
inputs.description: fork: the task whose active head the new branch derives from.

inputs.name: new_task_id
inputs.description: fork: the new branch task id (its own single active head; namespace inherited, never widened).

inputs.name: allowed_namespaces
inputs.description: The caller's namespace REQUEST (task_input.namespace analog). effective = intersection(request, grant).

inputs.name: permission_grants
inputs.description: The caller's control-plane namespace GRANT. Neither request nor grant widens the other.

inputs.name: record_kind
inputs.description: search: proves the boundary -- record_kind=working is never retrievable via search.

outputs.description: put_state: { op, task_id, namespace_scope, working_state_id, record_version_id, state_version, parent_state_version, content_hash, active_head_version, ns_policy_id, namespace_violation_count, records_digest } + artifact state.json (the working record envelope). get_active_head: { op, task_id, found, working_state_id?, state_version?, content_hash?, reason? } (+ state.json when found). list_by_task: { op, task_id, count, versions[] } (+ records.json). fork: { op, source_task_id, new_task_id, forked_from, state_version } (+ state.json). close|archive: { op, task_id, changed, lifecycle_state }. promote: { op, task_id, promoted_record_id, promoted_record_version_id, derives_from, promoted_record_kind=summary, working_record_unchanged } (+ promoted.json, source_working_state.json). search: { op, count=0, working_excluded_from_search=true, reason }. All access-controlled ops also carry namespace_violation_count + namespace_closure_violated (sanitized). Canonical record artifacts (state.json/records.json/promoted.json) are UTF-8 no BOM, sorted keys, byte-identical on a re-run of the same op sequence; identifying rejection detail goes to a privileged ns-security-log.jsonl (never returned).
